_: TEMPLATE for a record in data/potentials.json. THE ONE RULE THAT CATCHES PEOPLE: this is the only file in the materials module holding a number the app did not compute, so it is the only one where a citation is mandatory rather than good practice. A row you cannot trace to a document does not go in — not even a value everybody knows.
_couple: The half-reaction AS WRITTEN IN THE SOURCE, in the direction the source writes it (reduction). The written form is what decides pHIndependent below, so do not tidy it.
_symbol: Short label for the plot. Keep it under about twelve characters or it collides with its neighbours.

e0._value: The number, as a number. Used for arithmetic only.
e0._provenance: Always 'literature' here. A potential is a measurement, never theoretical, and this platform does not measure any.
e0._sourceId: A key in this file's top-level `sources` map. An id that names nothing is an ERROR in the health check and in tools/materials-test.mjs — it is worse than no citation, because it looks like one. Use `source` with the citation written out instead if the source is used only once.
e0._printed: The value EXACTLY as the source prints it, minus sign U+2212. The view displays this string and never a reformatted number: the source's precision is a claim about the measurement, and rounding K⁺/K to three decimals would invent a digit nobody measured. The test checks that this string and `value` agree.

_chemistry: Element symbols, as in materials.json. Use 'H2O' for the solvent limits.
_kind: 'metal' (M^n+ / M) · 'conversion' (a solid product, e.g. a sulfate or hydroxide) · 'solventLimit' (the water lines themselves — those are drawn differently and take `limit` and `pHSlope` instead of the pH fields below).
_pHIndependent: TRUE ONLY IF THE WRITTEN REACTION CONTAINS NO H⁺, NO OH⁻ AND NO H₂O. Those are drawn as a horizontal line across the whole pH axis. Everything else moves with pH — PbO₂/PbSO₄ carries four protons and moves about twice as fast as the water lines — and drawing one of those flat is the standard way a plot like this goes wrong: it puts the electrode on the wrong side of the window. When false, give definedAtPH instead.
_definedAtPH: For a pH-dependent couple: the pH its tabulated value is defined at. It is then plotted as a single point there rather than as a line, and the table beside the plot says 'only at pH N' instead of a verdict.
note: Optional. What this potential explains — the reason it is worth having in the file at all. Keep it to the thing a student would not work out alone.
